clue.text: Drinks and a sandwich

definitions.meaning: a set of drinks bought for everyone at the table in a pub
a sandwich made from two whole slices of bread

explanation.definitionFit: One buys a round of drinks for a group, and a round is also one complete sandwich made from two slices of bread.

clue.text: On a winding road it shows skill

indicators.note: a winding road twists about, so its letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Negotiating a twisty road demonstrates a driver's skill.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a driver on a twisting road; 'shows skill' is a loose adjectival definition, as in 'adroit' describing one who shows skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means dexterous or clever, describing someone who displays expertise.

clue.text: Company worker needs strict control

parts.note: a firm is a business company
a hand is a manual worker, as on a farm or ship

explanation.surface: A firm's employee requires firm discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruling with a firm hand is an idiom for keeping strict discipline.

clue.text: What winter sportsmen may need to reach their peak

definitions.text: What winter sportsmen may need to reach their peak

parts.words: What winter sportsmen may need to reach their peak
parts.note: reads like advice on athletes hitting top form, but literally describes the cable device that carries skiers up a mountain summit

explanation.surface: Athletes in winter events need something to help them hit top form.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable-hauled tow or chair carries skiers up the slope towards the summit.

clue.text: Some pressure in factory with single refreshment counter

parts.note: a mill is a factory, such as a cotton mill
I is the Roman numeral one
a bar is a counter serving drinks

explanation.surface: Pressure in a factory with one canteen counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A millibar is a unit of atmospheric pressure, a thousandth of a bar, so it measures some pressure.

clue.text: Skinny, toothless what's-his-name

parts.note: thin means skinny
a toothless mouth shows only gums, so it is gummy

explanation.surface: A description of a gaunt, gap-mouthed fellow whose name escapes you.
explanation.definitionFit: A word used for a person or thing whose name one cannot recall, like whatsit.

clue.text: Fools bat through the covers

indicators.note: one word goes right through the middle of the other, so it is placed inside

parts.note: hoods are covers, as for heads or prams
to bat an eyelid is to wink or blink

explanation.surface: A cricket batsman foolishly hits the ball through the covers fielding area.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket imagery: the covers is a fielding position off-side of the batsman. Here 'bat' is a blink and 'covers' are hoods.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoodwink someone is to deceive or trick them, making fools of them.

clue.text: A fair solution to the clue?

definitions.meaning: pale in colour, as fair hair or a pale complexion
in crosswords the word entered in the grid is called this

explanation.definitionFit: Light means pale in colour like fair hair, and crossword setters call each grid answer a light.

clue.text: A stretcher, to boot

parts.note: 'to boot' seems to mean 'as well', but it means a device put into footwear to stretch or hold its shape

explanation.surface: Also, a stretcher, as though adding one more item to a medical list.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe tree or boot tree is a shaped insert that keeps footwear stretched to shape.

clue.text: Teach a pupil without discipline

parts.note: to inform is to impart knowledge, to teach
L is a learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A teacher instructs an unruly pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual, relaxed and not bound by rules or formality, so lacking discipline.

clue.text: Give way concerning a fast time

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Yielding on the matter of a quick lap time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' suggests speed, but it is abstaining from food.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften and yield, giving in after resisting.

clue.text: It has caused many deaths in Vietnam

indicators.note: the answer sits within the letters of the following place name

explanation.surface: A remark about a war that killed many in Vietnam.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to war; the definition is a Sicilian volcano whose eruptions have killed many.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the Sicilian volcano whose eruptions have killed many people over history.

clue.text: Have a touch of colour and be miserable

parts.note: to feel is to touch
blue is a colour

explanation.surface: Have a dab of paint and be sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue is an idiom for being sad or depressed.

clue.text: Caught us, to face this sort of sentence

parts.note: c is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
taken as written
taken as written
a dial is the face of a clock

explanation.surface: Criminals caught and facing a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: A custodial sentence is one served in prison, in custody.

clue.text: Reserve team that will go down?

parts.note: a sub is a substitute or reserve player
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A second-string team facing relegation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a team being relegated; 'go down' means sink or settle.
explanation.definitionFit: To subside is to sink or abate, settling lower.

clue.text: Celebrated gent seen to take the initiative

parts.note: a star is a celebrated person
a toff is an upper-class gentleman

explanation.surface: A famous gentleman is seen to lead the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To start off is to begin, making the first move.

clue.text: Rouse MP into seeing C-in-C

indicators.note: turning one thing into another changes its form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Stirring a politician to see the Commander-in-Chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rouse' looks like the instruction; 'into' is, with ROUSE and MP the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is an overall chief, like a commander-in-chief.

clue.text: A foreign dignitary lacking credit

parts.note: un is 'a' in French
a worthy is a notable person

explanation.surface: A visiting foreign VIP without credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Unworthy means not deserving of praise or esteem.

clue.text: No one has time to set up the paper

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting up means lifting, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
tide is an old word for time, as in Yuletide

explanation.surface: Nobody has time to put the newspaper together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to set up' reverses the whole run NO+I+TIDE, read upwards in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one issue of a newspaper.

clue.text: Held firmly and beaten

definitions.meaning: fastened with a belt or band

explanation.definitionFit: Secured by a buckled band, or thrashed with a leather belt.

clue.text: Pea-jackets?

parts.note: a pea jacket is a sailor's coat, but read literally it is the casing that holds peas

explanation.surface: Asking about a sailor's short woollen coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The husks or shells enclosing peas.

clue.text: River sport

definitions.meaning: the ... flows through Durham in north-east England
to sport clothing is to have it on

explanation.definitionFit: The Wear is a river in north-east England, and to sport a garment is to have it on.

clue.text: Mixes up a signal and gets into a row

indicators.note: mixing up jumbles the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confuses a signal and joins a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but means a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To align things is to bring them into a straight line.

clue.text: Money raised by word of mouth

indicators.note: spoken rather than written, so the word is heard aloud

parts.note: bred means raised, as children or livestock

explanation.surface: Funds raised by verbal appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' looks like collecting money, but means brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for cash.

clue.text: Revised point I'd put to Edward

parts.note: E is a compass point, east

indicators.note: the two letters are put in a different order, here placed the other way round

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: An amended argument offered to a man named Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' is a mild signal here: the two letters of I'd are put the other way round before the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Edited means corrected or amended for publication.

clue.text: Rows about stray dogs

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, so the second is placed inside it

parts.note: tiers are rows, as of seats
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: Quarrels over stray dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' reads as quarrels and 'stray' as an adjective for dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Terriers are a group of small, lively breeds of dog.

clue.text: Is no longer providing admission for homeless children

indicators.note: admitting something lets it in, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: was is the past tense of is, what no longer is
if means providing, on condition that

explanation.surface: A shelter no longer admitting homeless children.
explanation.definitionFit: Waifs are neglected or abandoned young people with nowhere to live.

clue.text: Western hero with superlative steed

parts.note: suggests a cowboy film star, but recalls Walter Scott's ballad of the knight who came out of the west and whose steed was the best

explanation.surface: A cowboy hero riding the finest horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Scott's poem in Marmion begins 'O, young Lochinvar is come out of the west', and says 'his steed was the best'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dashing knight of Scott's ballad Marmion, who rides from the west on the best of horses.
